title: Shattered Lives: A Brutal Murder, A Cop On The Edge
author: Konrad Marshall
target_audience: Readers interested in true crime stories
Those keen on police procedural narratives
General nonfiction readers seeking gripping real-life stories
core_themes: Impact of violent crime on victims’ families and community
The resilience and breaking point of law enforcement officers
primary_purpose: To provide a meticulous, humanized account of a shocking murder case in Australia, exploring its far-reaching effects on the victims’ loved ones, the community, and especially the detective at the heart of the investigation.

structure_format.narrative_style: Narrative nonfiction, immersive, empathetic, and investigative
structure_format.organization: Follows a chronological structure interspersed with in-depth character backgrounds and thematic reflections
features: Personal interviews with investigators and affected families
Psychological exploration of the detective's journey
Contextual analysis of the case's impact

key_concepts_lessons: Violent crimes create ripples of trauma extending well beyond the immediate victims.
Detectives and police officers carry emotional and psychological burdens that can deeply impact their lives.
Systemic challenges within law enforcement can influence the pursuit of justice.
Society often underestimates the lasting impact of unspeakable crimes.
Personal resilience and the search for meaning are vital in facing tragedy and loss.
notable_features: Focus on the detective's internal struggles as well as the crime itself
In-depth, journalistic reporting with a strong empathic approach
Rich sense of place—conveys the unique atmosphere of an Australian community
Balances procedural detail with human stories
cultural_historical_context: Set against the backdrop of contemporary Australia, the book sheds light on the pressures faced by modern law enforcement and the ongoing crisis of violent crime. It situates the narrative within a national conversation about policing, trauma, and community healing.
reception_impact: Acclaimed for its detailed, sensitive writing and deep psychological insight
Read widely in Australia’s true crime community and among fans of thoughtful nonfiction
Highlighted by reviewers for humanizing both victims and investigators
Considered a significant addition to Australian true crime literature
comparable_titles: The Trauma Cleaner by Sarah Krasnostein
The Killing Season: Uncut by Sarah Ferguson
The Short and Excruciatingly Embarrassing Reign of Captain Abbott by Andrew P Street (for Australian political/crime context)
